title: Flow dial: Draft, Copilot or Autopilot for each flow
description: Give every flow a dial with three stops, set only by the Owner with the CLI token. Draft (the default) only drafts, and every item waits for the Owner. Copilot acts only after the Owner approves each item. Autopilot runs all the time: Core still never sends or publishes, and instead hands finished items to a sending app outside Core that the Owner has already approved. Draft and Copilot need a spend cap; Autopilot does not. Moving a flow to Autopilot is bound to a hash of its channel list and caps, so changing either holds the flow until the Owner confirms again. The kill switch, the Supervisor pause and the stall breaker hold a flow at every stop, and the dial never raises a stream above the global L3 ceiling or changes the core policy for publish_external, outbound_email_external or spend_money. The hand-off outbox itself, and the sending app, are later work. Owner decision 10 Nov: Autopilot hands off to a sender outside Core.
acceptance: GET /v1/supervisor shows each flow's dial; a fresh flow is at draft
Only the CLI token can set the dial; without it the request answers 401 and nothing changes; each change writes a system.config_changed event naming the flow and the stop
Setting autopilot without the current confirm hash answers 409 with that hash and changes nothing; with it, the flow is at autopilot
When a flow at autopilot changes its channel list or caps, it is held by dial_unapproved until the Owner confirms the new hash
At draft and copilot a flow with no dollar cap is held by cap_required; at autopilot it is not
The kill switch holds a flow at autopilot by kill_switch
fw supervisor status --json prints the same dial for each flow
The web UI shows each flow's dial on the Flows page with no horizontal scroll at 390 px
